READ_THIS_FIRST.instruction_for_ai: DO NOT calculate totals from individual activities. Use the pre-calculated values in 'summary', 'weekly_summary', and 'derived_metrics' sections below. These are already computed accurately from the API data.
READ_THIS_FIRST.display_formatting: For durations and sleep, always display the '_formatted' fields (e.g., sleep_formatted, duration_formatted, total_training_formatted) instead of converting decimal '_hours' values. The formatted fields are pre-calculated from raw seconds and avoid rounding errors.
READ_THIS_FIRST.extended_data_note: ACWR and baselines calculated from 28 days of data
READ_THIS_FIRST.capability_metrics_note: The 'capability' block in derived_metrics contains durability trend (aggregate decoupling 7d/28d), efficiency factor trend (aggregate EF 7d/28d), HRRc trend (heart rate recovery 7d/28d), TID comparison (7d vs 28d distribution drift), power curve delta (MMP shift at anchor durations across 28d windows — energy system adaptation direction), HR curve delta (max sustained HR shift at anchor durations — cardiac adaptation, cross-sport), sustainability profile (per-sport power/HR sustainability table for race estimation — 42d window, sport-filtered), and DFA a1 profile (per-session non-linear HRV index from AlphaHRV Connect IQ field — latest_session + trailing_by_sport with crossing-band LT1/LT2 estimates). These measure HOW the athlete expresses fitness, not just load. Use these for coaching context alongside traditional load metrics. Durability and EF trend direction matters more than absolute values. HRRc is display only — higher = better parasympathetic recovery. Power curve delta rotation_index reveals whether gains are sprint-biased (positive) or endurance-biased (negative). HR curve delta is ambiguous — rising max sustained HR may indicate fitness or fatigue; cross-reference with resting HRV/HR and RPE. Sustainability profile provides race estimation lookup: actual MMP, Coggan predicted (cycling only), CP/W' model (cycling only), model_divergence_pct (actual vs CP — divergence IS the coaching signal). CP/W' is primary for durations ≤20min; Coggan duration factors are the established reference for ≥60min. Source flag (observed_outdoor/observed_indoor) matters for cycling race estimation — indoor MMP is typically 3-5% lower. DFA a1 profile: thresholds (1.0 ≈ LT1, 0.5 ≈ LT2) cycling-validated only — non-cycling sports get rollups but validated=False. Crossing-band estimates: HR is pooled across all sessions; watts are split by environment for cycling (watts_outdoor, watts_indoor with per-environment n_sessions) — compare watts_outdoor against ftp, watts_indoor against ftp_indoor. Non-cycling sports keep pooled watts. Estimates are provisional at confidence='low' (suppressed for calibration delta surfacing) and usable at 'moderate' or 'high'. DFA a1 is a Tier-2 interpretive signal — does NOT enter readiness P0–P3 ladder, does NOT auto-update dossier zones; surfaces calibration deltas only. Quality gate: refuse to interpret when latest_session.sufficient=false or trailing confidence=null. See SECTION_11.md DFA a1 Protocol for full interpretation rules.
READ_THIS_FIRST.readiness_decision_note: The 'readiness_decision' block contains a pre-computed go/modify/skip recommendation with priority level (P0=safety, P1=overload, P2=fatigue, P3=green), individual signal statuses, phase-adjusted thresholds, and structured modification guidance. Use this as the baseline for pre-workout recommendations. Override with explanation in the coach note if the AI's contextual judgment disagrees.

wellness_field_scales.note: All categorical wellness fields use a 1-4 positional scale where 1 = best state, 4 = worst state. Labels differ per field but direction is consistent. Fields are null when not reported.
wellness_field_scales.menstrual: menstrual_phase and menstrual_phase_predicted are not on the 1-4 scale. Values: PERIOD, FOLLICULAR, OVULATION, LUTEAL, etc.

readiness_decision.reason: P3 green light. 6 green, 0 amber (threshold 3), 0 red.

derived_metrics.grey_zone_note: Gray Zone % (Z3/tempo) - minimize in polarized training
derived_metrics.quality_intensity_note: Quality Intensity % (Z4+/threshold+) - target ~20% in polarized training
derived_metrics.easy_time_ratio_note: Easy time (Z1+Z2) / Total - target ~80% in polarized training
derived_metrics.hard_days_note: Power ladder: z3+ >= 30min, z4+ >= 10min, z5+ >= 5min, z6+ >= 2min, z7 >= 1min. HR fallback (when no power): z4+ >= 10min, z5+ >= 5min. Per Seiler 3-zone model + Foster. HR-based days flagged with intensity_basis: hr

durability.reliability_note: insufficient qualifying sessions for alert evaluation: 7d N=1 (min 3), 28d N=4 (min 5)
durability.note: Steady-state power sessions only (VI <= 1.05, VI > 0, >= 90min, power data). Negative decoupling = strong durability. Trend compares 7d vs 28d mean (+/-1% = stable). Alerts require N28>=5 (alarm) or N7>=3 AND N28>=5 (declining warning) for statistical reliability.

efficiency_factor.note: Steady-state cycling sessions only (VI <= 1.05, VI > 0, >= 20min, power+HR data). Rising EF = improving aerobic efficiency. Compare like-for-like sessions only — EF varies with intensity. Trend compares 7d vs 28d mean (+/-0.03 = stable).

hrrc.note: HRRc = heart rate recovery (largest 60s HR drop in bpm after exceeding threshold HR for >1 min). Higher = better parasympathetic recovery. Null when threshold not reached, recording stopped before cooldown, or no HR data. Trend: 7d mean vs 28d mean, >10% = meaningful (min 1 session/7d, 3 sessions/28d). Display only — not wired into readiness_decision signals.

tid_comparison.note: Compares 7d vs 28d Seiler TID to detect distribution shifts. pi_delta positive = more polarized acutely.

power_curve_delta.note: Compares MMP at 5 anchor durations (5s neuromuscular, 60s anaerobic, 300s MAP, 1200s threshold, 3600s endurance) across two 28d windows. rotation_index = mean(5s,60s pct_change) - mean(1200s,3600s pct_change). Positive = sprint-biased gains, negative = endurance-biased. 300s excluded from rotation (transitional). Null when either window has fewer than 3 valid anchor durations.

hr_curve_delta.note: Compares max sustained HR at 4 anchor durations (60s anaerobic ceiling, 300s VO2max HR, 1200s threshold HR, 3600s endurance HR) across two 28d windows. rotation_index = mean(60s,300s pct_change) - mean(1200s,3600s pct_change). Positive = intensity-biased HR shift, negative = endurance-biased. No sport filter — HR is cross-sport physiological (dominated by hardest efforts). IMPORTANT: rising max sustained HR is ambiguous — may indicate improved cardiac output (good) or accumulated fatigue/dehydration/heat (bad). Cross-reference with resting HRV, resting HR, RPE, and environmental context before interpreting. Null when either window has fewer than 3 valid anchor durations.

cycling.model_trust_note: CP/W' model (P=CP+W'/t) is primary for durations ≤20min where W' contribution is meaningful. Coggan duration factors (Allen & Coggan, 3rd ed.) are the established reference for ≥60min. 30min is the crossover zone where both apply. model_divergence_pct = (actual - CP_model) / CP_model × 100. Positive divergence at short durations may indicate strong anaerobic capacity or stale W' value. Indoor MMP is typically 3-5% lower than outdoor (cooling, motivation) — source flag indicates which environment produced each anchor.

planned_workouts.name: P1 W36 CONSOLIDATION - Long Aerobic Endurance 2h30
planned_workouts.description:
Macro phase: Phase 1 — Threshold re-entry and durability rebuild (2026 W33–W36).

Section 11 basis: AE-1 Steady-State Endurance, shortened for consolidation week.
Adaptation target: retain long-ride frequency and aerobic durability while reducing duration by 30 minutes versus loading weeks.

- 20m 55-65% FTP
- 110m 65-70% FTP
- 20m 55-65% FTP

Strictly aerobic with no tempo finish. Fuel at 90 g carbohydrate/hour. If readiness is adverse or leg soreness exceeds 2/10, shorten to 2 hours rather than adding intensity.

planned_workouts.name: P2 W37 HARD - Indoor ERG Sweet Spot 2x27 80min
planned_workouts.description:
Macro phase: Phase 2 — Aerobic base and strength foundation (2026 W37–W44).

Section 11 basis: SS-1 Sustained Sweet Spot Blocks (adapted to 2 x 27 minutes).
Adaptation target: sustained aerobic power and muscular endurance as the primary of two separated loading-week cycling quality opportunities.

Accepted setting: indoor FTP 254 W. Every steady ERG step uses one exact %FTP target; 90% = 229 W in the aligned MyWhoosh profile. No FTP or threshold setting is changed by this workout.
Evidence-based progression: the completed 2026-08-28 indoor 2 x 25 minutes averaged 228 / 228 W, cadence 98 / 99, whole-session RPE 6, Feel 2, neutral response and no power fade. This therefore progresses duration only to 2 x 27 rather than repeating a demonstrated loading dose.

- 10m 50% FTP
- 5m 65% FTP
- 27m 90% FTP
- 5m 50% FTP
- 27m 90% FTP
- 6m 50% FTP

Use MyWhoosh ERG with normal cooling. RPE target 7–8; hold cadence steady and do not raise the second interval. Collect HR/DFA passively; automatic crossings do not set FTP/LTHR.
Progression gate: both intervals should remain stable, cadence controlled and whole-session RPE no higher than 8. If the consolidation block leaves unresolved fatigue or current readiness is adverse, repeat the completed 2 x 25 structure rather than forcing the extension.
Readiness gate: Section 11 daily readiness overrides the calendar. Do not repay reduced or missed work later in the week.

planned_workouts.name: P2 W37 - Home Strength Foundation 35min
planned_workouts.description:
Macro phase: Phase 2 — Aerobic base and strength foundation (2026 W37–W44).

Section 11 basis: individualized home-strength foundation; the cycling workout library does not prescribe strength loading.
Adaptation target: test whether a repeatable bodyweight home-strength exposure is viable before buying equipment or attempting externally loaded progression.

CONFIRMED EQUIPMENT — pull-up bar only. No dumbbells, plates, bands, bench, sliders or loaded backpack are assumed.
- Bodyweight split squat: 2 x 8–12 per side
- Single-leg hip bridge: 2 x 8–12 per side
- Hamstring walkout from bridge: 2 x 6–10
- Push-up: 2 x 8–15
- Pull-up or chin-up: 2 submaximal sets; stop with about 3–4 repetitions in reserve
- Single-leg calf raise: 2 x 12–20 per side
- Side plank: 2 x 30–45 seconds per side

Use normal household floor space and stable furniture only when needed for balance; furniture is not a loading prescription. No failure, grinders, deliberate soreness or improvised unstable loading. Use controlled range of motion and normal rests. Planned duration: 35 minutes.

W37 is the first loading-week repetition. Repeat the W36 movements rather than adding difficulty unless W36 caused no meaningful 24–48-hour soreness and no cycling interference.

Viability/progression rule: record completed repetitions and hardest-set RIR for each movement, pull-up/chin-up grip and repetitions, any pain, actual session duration/setup friction, and next-day lower-body soreness. Progress only one variable after a clean 24–48-hour response. If the top of a repetition range remains far from challenging, label that movement load-limited rather than inventing more work; that evidence informs whether external load is needed.
Readiness gate: Section 11 daily readiness and cycling quality take priority. Stop or simplify lower-body work for pain, altered mechanics, meaningful residual fatigue or adverse cycling response. Do not repay reduced work later in the week.

If repetitions/RIR, soreness or cycling response are missing, the coach must not infer progression from duration or strength TSS; repeat or hold until evidence exists.

planned_workouts.name: P2 W37 CONDITIONAL QUALITY - Outdoor Sweet Spot 3x10 60min
planned_workouts.description:
Macro phase: Phase 2 — Aerobic base and strength foundation (2026 W37–W44).

Section 11 basis: SS-1 Sustained Sweet Spot Blocks, adapted outdoors to a shorter 3 x 10 minute secondary quality stimulus.
Adaptation target: provide the second separated cycling-quality opportunity required in P2 loading weeks without matching the duration or cost of Tuesday’s primary 2 x 25 minute session.

OUTDOOR EXECUTION — provisional outdoor FTP 265 W:
- 10m at 50–65% FTP = 133–172 W
- 10m at 86–90% FTP = 228–239 W
- 5m at 50–60% FTP = 133–159 W
- 10m at 86–90% FTP = 228–239 W
- 5m at 50–60% FTP = 133–159 W
- 10m at 86–90% FTP = 228–239 W
- 10m at 50–60% FTP = 133–159 W

Settle mainly around 232–236 W during the work when terrain permits. RPE target 6–7; controlled breathing and stable mechanics, with no hard final minute. Normal brief outdoor variation is acceptable, but do not chase average power after junctions or descents.

CONDITIONAL GATE: perform this secondary quality session only if Tuesday’s primary session finished at RPE no higher than 8, there is no meaningful residual lower-body soreness from strength, and readiness is supportive. Otherwise retain the original 60-minute aerobic fallback: 10m at 50–60%, 40m at 60–68%, 10m at 50–60%. Do not compensate later. Sunday remains strictly aerobic.

planned_workouts.name: P2 W37 - Easy Run — Impact Maintenance 45min
planned_workouts.description:
Macro phase: Phase 2 — Aerobic base and strength foundation (2026 W37–W44).

Section 11 basis: individualized secondary-sport impact maintenance; no exact run template exists in the cycling-focused workout library.
Adaptation target: preserve impact familiarity and reduce future running restart cost without competing with cycling development.

Execution: 5-minute easy warm-up, 35 minutes at 6:25–6:55/km on flat predictable terrain, then 5-minute easy cool-down. RPE 2–3 and conversational throughout.
Start only with normal walking/stairs, no pain at rest and no focal shin/ankle tenderness. Stop for focal or increasing pain, pain above 2/10, or gait change. Pace is the default target; RPE and symptoms override it.
This preserves general impact tolerance, not half-marathon-specific durability. Do not add cycling to compensate if this run is shortened or skipped.
Readiness gate: Section 11 daily readiness overrides the calendar. Do not repay reduced or missed work later in the week.

planned_workouts.name: P2 W39 SCAFFOLD — Load 3
planned_workouts.description_preview:
Macro phase: Phase 2 — Aerobic base and strength foundation (2026 W37–W44).
Status: provisional loading-week scaffold only — not an exact workout prescription. Daily placement, exact hours, dose and descriptive TSS must be rebuilt from fresh history, current same-domain workout evidence, athlete feedback and Section 11 readiness at the named adaptation checkpoint.
Architecture: use the agreed 6–8 total-hour availability, normally with two separated cycling quality slots at least 48 hours apart and no back-to-back hard days. One slot is a sustained-power progression; the secondary stimulus is selected after W38 evidence. A hard group ride may replace, never supplement, the secondary slot.

planned_workouts.description_preview:
Macro phase: Phase 2 — Aerobic base and strength foundation (2026 W37–W44).
Status: provisional consolidation-week scaffold only — not an exact workout prescription. Daily placement, exact hours, dose and descriptive TSS must be rebuilt after the W37–W39 block review.
Architecture: preserve familiar training frequency within the agreed 6–8-hour availability while reducing the actual dose relative to the completed loading block. Retain one shortened cycling quality touch, no second hard slot and no back-to-back hard days.
